text: Fodor's productivity argument holds that because we can entertain an unbounded number of novel thoughts using finitely many concepts, thought must have a generative, combinatorial structure.
explanation: True: the productivity argument holds that since we can think indefinitely many novel thoughts (e.g., about 17,342 grains of sand) from a finite stock of concepts, thought must have a generative, combinatorial structure - exactly what a formal language (LOT) supplies. It is the companion of the systematicity argument.
